reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an Ethereum front-running bot as an automated way to earn substantial recurring returns, including claims of more than $1,000 per day and 3 to 6 Ether per week. It instructs viewers to pay network fees and transfer Ethereum into the contract, presents larger deposits as enabling larger profits, and directs them to obtain the source code through the speaker's Fiverr profile. The displayed balance and variable-return disclaimer do not verify the claimed profits, the bot's operation, or recovery of deposited funds.

citations.quote: My Ethereum Front Running bot earns profits on the Autopilot.
Please check out the step-by-step tutorial to see how easy it is to actually run it.
It takes advantage of decentralized finance platforms to sandwich transactions for arbitrage.
This will allow us to process our order first, then process a sell order right after, in the same blockchain block.
the next step is to fund the contract with Ethereum

opening.argument: Judge the earnings claim in the context of the speaker's own qualifications. He says profits fluctuate, explains that deploying the contract requires gas fees, and describes funding as an amount the viewer chooses. Those details do not prove the bot works, but they are more consistent with a discussion of a variable, costly trading activity than with a promise that every viewer will receive a fixed payout.

citations.quote: The profits will fluctuate week to week.
Gas fees are the commission on the Ethereum Network for smart contract deployment.
You can fund the contract with whatever amount of Ethereum you want

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution quotes the bot's claimed profits and trading mechanism, but neither quote establishes a guaranteed return. Its funding quote establishes that the tutorial calls for Ethereum to be sent to a contract; it does not, by itself, establish that the speaker controls that contract or that deposited funds cannot be withdrawn. The speaker expressly says returns fluctuate.

citations.quote: The profits will fluctuate week to week.
the next step is to fund the contract with Ethereum

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Variable returns and disclosed gas fees do not answer the central concern. The speaker urges viewers to fund the contract, says larger deposits can produce more profit, and claims a gain of more than half his deposit in about a day. A qualification about weekly fluctuations does not verify the bot's operation or make that funding pitch reliable.

citations.quote: the more you put in, the larger the transactions you will be able to sandwich and the more profit you can accumulate over time.
it basically took me a day to gain over half my deposit back.

opening.argument: This is substantially an operational walkthrough: the speaker explains what Remix is, identifies a Solidity compiler version, and describes the contract controls, including a withdrawal function. The viewer is shown a sequence of development and deployment steps, not merely an invitation to hand money to an unnamed operator. The demonstration cannot independently prove the reported profits, but the technical instruction is central to what the video presents.

citations.quote: Remix is a Web3 application that allows us to develop, compile, deploy, and launch smart contracts coded in the Solidity language.
under compiler select the 0.6 version
Withdraw stops the bot and transfers the funds back into your wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the tutorial includes funding and profit claims. But its excerpts omit the sustained attention to creating, compiling and deploying a contract, as well as the described withdrawal control. Calling the demonstration a solicitation alone does not account for those instructional steps; nor does the inability to verify a reported balance establish that no instruction is taking place.

citations.quote: Paste the code into the file bot.sole This is our slippage bot.
now click on the compile bot soul button and wait for the bot to compile
Withdraw stops the bot and transfers the funds back into your wallet.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical steps can be part of a promotion. Here they lead to funding the contract, after which the speaker reports rapid gains and tells viewers to obtain his source code. A described withdrawal button is not proof that a viewer's deposited Ethereum will be returned. The walkthrough makes the earnings pitch actionable rather than removing it.

citations.quote: the next step is to fund the contract with Ethereum
Nice, it's a little over 1.6 Ethereum so it basically took me a day to gain over half my deposit back.
Just head over to my Fiverr profile, link in the description, and get the source code today.

opening.argument: The speaker directs viewers toward bot source code and describes using their own wallet to deploy a contract. That can be read as promotion of a tool or service, not evidence that viewers must pay the speaker for a guaranteed return. The supplied account does call for funding the contract, but it does not establish the terms on which the code is provided, show a request for wallet credentials, or establish who ultimately controls the deployed contract. Those missing facts matter before treating the code promotion itself as a deceptive transfer scheme.

citations.quote: Just head over to my Fiverr profile, link in the description, and get the source code today.
so now we're going to deploy this to our wallet.
the next step is to fund the contract with Ethereum

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited instructions establish deployment and funding, but not that the speaker receives the funded Ethereum. Likewise, the claims about sandwich trades describe a proposed trading mechanism; those excerpts do not reveal the contract's actual behavior. The Fiverr direction is a route to obtain code, with no stated price or payment terms in that invitation. Suspicion about an external code source is reasonable, but these particular excerpts leave the alleged transfer mechanism unproven.

citations.quote: It takes advantage of decentralized finance platforms to sandwich transactions for arbitrage.
Just head over to my Fiverr profile, link in the description, and get the source code today.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern does not depend on proving a Fiverr price or seeing a credential request. The speaker instructs viewers to fund the contract, links larger funding to larger profits, and reports a striking one-day gain before urging them to obtain the code. The supplied material does not verify that the contract performs the claimed trades or returns viewers' funds, so describing the code as an ordinary product does not resolve the risk created by the earnings pitch.
